name: Typebot
tagline: Block-based chatbot that looks like a form and is easy to edit
description: Block-based chatbot builder that users see as a form, with self-hosting possible, WhatsApp integration and a webhook to connect any AI.
priceNote: Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Support with a guided form that does not scare the customer away
pros: The bot looks like a filled-in form, which sharply reduces drop-off compared with feeling like a robot
Visual block editor, and the sales team builds the flow alone in an afternoon
Self-hosted open source and free, which solves both the data and the cost question
Webhook and API to plug in whichever AI you want, without being locked to one model
cons: Self-hosting requires a server, a domain, SSL and someone who upgrades the Typebot version
No built-in AI: to answer with a language model you have to integrate one through a webhook
Meta's WhatsApp API is billed per delivered message, and that cost sits outside the subscription
Fewer ready integrations than ManyChat and Zapier, which means more manual connection work

features.name: Block editor
features.detail: Snaps question, option, file and button cards into a sequence

features.name: Website embed
features.detail: Bot appears as a window or button on any page, with no SDK

features.name: Webhooks and API
features.detail: Sends the answers to your AI or backend and returns the response

features.name: Connected channels
features.detail: Website, Messenger, Slack, Discord and WhatsApp, the last one on paid plans

features.name: Self-hosted open source
features.detail: Runs with Docker on your infrastructure, with no monthly fee and full brand customization

useCases: Post-sale data collection that opens the ticket in the CRM with a summary of the conversation
Support triage on the website before handing the customer to a human team
Lead qualification with staged questions and delivery to a spreadsheet or CRM
Satisfaction survey in three questions after the order, with the score recorded in your system
bestForWho: Companies that want a website chatbot that looks like a form and prefer to self-host instead of depending on a platform.
verdict: Typebot solves a problem ManyChat does not: a bot that looks like a form, which cuts drop-off on website support and booking flows. The block editor is fast, and the sales team can change it without asking a developer, which is rare in this market. What it lacks is ready-made intelligence: to understand a question in natural language you connect a model through a webhook, and then quality depends on what you build. For a small company, self-hosting with Docker on your own domain works and costs almost nothing, adding only the WhatsApp API when you use it. For a larger company, the cloud version saves you the operations, and it is worth comparing cost per conversation with ManyChat before you decide.
